findings.message: specs/city-data/spec.md, requirement "Coordinates of the GeoNames cities", says: "The compile command MUST stop without writing the file when a city row has no latitude or longitude or one out of range." No task in tasks.md implements or tests the out-of-range part. Task 3.1 only makes parseGeoNamesRows throw on "an empty or non-numeric value", and task 3.4 checks ranges only in checkCityData on the committed file. scripts/cityData/compile.ts:72-83 writes the dataset right after compileCityData with no check in between, so a GeoNames row with latitude 91 or longitude -181 would be written, which breaks the spec. Fix: extend task 3.1 (or 3.2) to reject out-of-range latitude and longitude at compile time, naming the line, with a test (and a scenario in task 3.6), or remove "or one out of range" from the requirement and the matching part of FR1.

findings.message: design.md Context claims `scripts/zoneRules/compileWithZic.ts` "unpacks only the nine source files and `version` from the signed tzdata archive"; the code does not do that: `compileArchive` runs `tar -xzf archivePath -C sourceDirectory`, unpacking the whole archive (zone.tab included); only the `zic` invocation is restricted to `TZDATA_SOURCE_FILES`. Task 4.2 ('unpack `zone.tab` with the source files') is built on this wrong claim and should instead read the already-extracted `zone.tab` from `sourceDirectory`.

tasks.md does not verify metric M3 as stated: M3 promises '10 of 10 sample city records carry exactly these coordinates', including the GeoNames city Quito −0.2, −78.5, but task 3.6 checks the committed city data only for the five cities of the spec's 'Sample cities of the committed city data' table (Kazan, Murmansk, Saint Petersburg, San Francisco, Mumbai, 'within 0.1°'). Quito is covered only by a synthetic compile fixture, so no task asserts M3's Quito record on the committed data, and the spec's 'within 0.1°' contradicts M3's 'exactly'. Align the spec table and task 3.6 with M3's ten records and wording.
